# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. 1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`

4. **Comment inaccuracy**: "the notification dispatches mid-layout" — actually the framework delays `ScrollMetricsNotification` to a microtask after the frame completes ("It is too late to send useful notifications... we delay it until after the frame is complete", scroll_position.dart). Actually wait — is the comment wrong? The notification IS scheduled during layout (scheduleMicrotask called from applyContentDimensions during layout), and dispatched in a microtask — microtasks run after the frame completes (actually microtasks run when the current event/microtask completes — during a frame, after each phase? Microtasks run between... In the Flutter frame pipeline, microtasks queued during layout run at the end of the current event loop turn, after the frame (drawFrame) completes since the whole frame runs synchronously in one task). So dispatch happens after the frame is complete, NOT mid-layout. The comment "the notification dispatches mid-layout" is inaccurate. But — hmm, is it worth flagging? It's a code comment that could mislead future maintainers. SUGGESTION-level.

5. **`_topBannerVisible` reads `_revealedNow` during build but the `Expanded`+`Column` layout**: when the banner visibility flips via setState from a scroll listener, fine.

6. **A subtle behavioral gap**: the reveal gate keys on `pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64`. But `_trackNearBottom`/`_trackUserScroll` use `pixels < 150` for near-bottom on the same reversed list. Consistent approach. OK.

7. **`ScrollMetricsNotification` listener + `depth != 0` guard**: verified correct semantics (depth counts viewports bubbled through; the nested inner NotificationListener doesn't increment). The guard correctly filters nested scrollables (e.g., tool output panes). No issue — actually this is well done.

8. **Post-frame callback accumulation**: every ScrollMetricsNotification schedules a post-frame callback; a paged-in page + layout can fire several per frame; each is trivial. `_updateTopReveal` no-ops when unchanged. Fine.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events

  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

Microtasks run between... In the Flutter frame pipeline, microtasks queued during layout run at the end of the current event loop turn, after the frame (drawFrame) completes since the whole frame runs synchronously in one task). So dispatch happens after the frame is complete, NOT mid-layout. The comment "the notification dispatches mid-layout" is inaccurate. But — hmm, is it worth flagging? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),

Now I fully understand the depth semantics:

- `ScrollMetricsNotification extends Notification with ViewportNotificationMixin`.
- `depth` counts **viewports** (elements mixing `ViewportElementMixin`, i.e., `ViewportElement` / `SingleChildViewportElement` — scrollable-viewport elements) the notification bubbled through. NotificationListener elements do NOT increment depth unless they also mix ViewportElementMixin.

So `notification.depth == 0` at the outer listener means the metrics notification came from the transcript's scrollable without passing through another viewport (scrollable) in between. The inner `NotificationListener<ScrollNotification>` is a plain NotifiableElementMixin — doesn't increment depth. So the guard works as intended. 

Also, from `scroll_position.dart:676`: `scheduleMicrotask(didUpdateScrollMetrics)` and the assert `schedulerPhase != SchedulerPhase.persistentCallbacks` — the dispatch happens in a microtask AFTER layout (not mid-layout). The code comment says "the notification dispatches mid-layout" — slightly inaccurate (it dispatches in a microtask after layout, scheduled from `applyContentDimensions` during layout), but the post-frame callback approach remains correct and safe. Actually wait — let me check line 676's context to be precise.

Also let me check `scrollable.dart:986` — `if (notification.depth == 0)` — the Scrollable's own handling. Not needed.

One more check: since ScrollMetricsNotification dispatches via microtask (not during build), calling `addPostFrameCallback` from the listener is fine, but they could have called `_updateTopReveal()` directly (setState in microtask is fine too). Using post-frame is safer anyway (avoids setState during layout if dispatch ever happened mid-layout). Fine.

Now — the assert at line 1076: `assert(SchedulerBinding.instance.schedulerPhase != SchedulerPhase.persistentCallbacks)`. The comment in the PR code says "post-framed — the notification dispatches mid-layout". The dispatch actually happens in a microtask. Confirmed: `ScrollMetricsNotification` is dispatched via microtask after the frame's layout completes (framework comment: "we delay it until after the frame is complete"). So the PR comment "the notification dispatches mid-layout" is slightly inaccurate — it dispatches in a microtask scheduled during layout, i.e., after the frame completes. That's why the assert forbids dispatching during persistentCallbacks. The post-frame callback wrapper is therefore strictly safe (double-deferred). Minor doc nit only.

Actually with a reversed list and centerKey etc., depends on the ChatAnimatedList implementation; but per E2E test, after paging the banner remains tappable in place ("turned into its terminal state in place"), so offset remains at the oldest edge. And `_updateTopReveal` re-measures via metrics notification. OK.

The PR acknowledges it ("One-frame settle"). Since `_syncMessages` is async (timer debounce), and the first build of the Chat might have the list attached already with extents measured in the same frame... Actually the flash scenario: build 1 with banner visible (hasClients false at that moment? `_chatScrollController.hasClients` false → reveal true → banner renders). First message sync → list attaches → frame lays out → post-frame callback → hides. So the banner is visible for ~1 frame at open on windowed sessions. Cosmetic and acknowledged. Now the exhaustive review pass. Let me re-read the changed files completely and surface ALL remaining issues.

Findings so far:

1. **One-frame flash of the banner at session open (windowed sessions with pages)** — `_topBannerRevealed = true` initial + `_revealedNow` returns true until extents measured → banner renders for ~1 frame before hiding at the live tail. Acknowledged in the PR description as a known tradeoff. SUGGESTION.

2. **Stale `_topBannerRevealed` never re-synced on service swap / initState** — `didUpdateWidget` re-syncs `_historyAbove` etc. but not `_topBannerRevealed`; however `_topBannerVisible` reads the live `_revealedNow`, so correctness is preserved; `_topBannerRevealed` only drives rebuilds. When the service swaps, `_syncMessages` runs → finally block schedules post-frame `_updateTopReveal` → resyncs. OK, no issue.

3. **`_updateTopReveal` registered via `addListener` but never explicitly removed** — controller disposed in dispose(), which detaches listeners. Same pattern as `_trackNearBottom`. Consistent with codebase. No issue.

4. **Comment inaccuracy**: "the notification dispatches mid-layout" — actually the framework delays `ScrollMetricsNotification` to a microtask after the frame completes ("It is too late to send useful notifications... we delay it until after the frame is complete", scroll_position.dart). The post-frame wrap is harmless (belt & braces), but the comment misstates the mechanism. Very minor doc nit — SUGGESTION.

Actually wait — is the comment wrong? The notification IS scheduled during layout (scheduleMicrotask called from applyContentDimensions during layout), and dispatched in a microtask — microtasks run after the frame completes (actually microtasks run when the current event/microtask completes — during a frame, after each phase? Microtasks run between... In the Flutter frame pipeline, microtasks queued during layout run at the end of the current event loop turn, after the frame (drawFrame) completes since the whole frame runs synchronously in one task). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

Microtasks run between... In the Flutter frame pipeline, microtasks queued during layout run at the end of the current event loop turn, after the frame (drawFrame) completes since the whole frame runs synchronously in one task). So dispatch happens after the frame is complete, NOT mid-layout. The comment "the notification dispatches mid-layout" is inaccurate. But — hmm, is it worth flagging? On the FIRST frame, the controller has no clients (list not built yet) → hasClients false → true → safe. On SUBSEQUENT frames where the screen rebuilds while the list is already laid out — dimensions exist → safe. The dangerous window: a frame where the screen rebuilds and the Scrollable was just attached in a previous frame but hasn't laid out — practically impossible since attach and layout happen within the same frame (build→layout). Hmm wait — attach happens during BUILD phase (position created in didChangeDependencies during build/inflate), layout runs after ALL builds in that same frame. So by the time ANY build runs again, the previous frame's layout has applied dimensions. Actually the sequence within a frame: build (attach, hasClients true, no dims) → layout (applyContentDimensions, dims set). So reading from build always sees dims from the previous frame's layout. UNLESS the scrollable was detached and reattached (e.g., `emptyChatListBuilder` swaps the list out — the ChatAnimatedList removed → position detached → hasClients false; re-added → attach during build → read during the NEXT build in the same... no, next build is a later frame).

Ancestor build reads controller state; descendant attach happens later in the same frame. So a read during build sees the state as of after the previous frame. Safe.

2. Post-frame callbacks — after layout → dims set (if hasClients). Safe. Actually careful: post-frame callback after the frame where the list was REMOVED from the tree: hasClients false → safe.

3. Scroll position listener — fires during drag/activity, dims exist. Safe... but what about `ScrollPosition` created fresh on a NEW position after a `ChatAnimatedList` recreation (e.g., theme change rebuilds, service swap)? The field assignment happens at the top: `hasContentDimensions` set true near the start (`_didChangeViewportDimensionOrReceiveCorrection = true`... let me not go down this hole — assignment of _maxScrollExtent happens in `applyContentDimensions` before `correctNewDimensions`...

So the missing `hasContentDimensions` guard is a theoretical robustness gap, not a live crash. The standard defensive pattern (`hasClients && position.hasContentDimensions` or try `position.hasPixels && position.hasContentDimensions`) would be strictly safer. Given all call sites are post-layout or guarded by hasClients with the attach→layout ordering making the race practically unreachable (build of ancestor can't interleave with a descendant's attach in the same frame... wait, actually it CAN: the Chat screen's build → descendant Chat builds → ChatAnimatedList created → position attached (build phase) → LAYOUT phase same frame applies dimensions → post-frame callback fires → safe. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

    "description": "Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched."
  }
}

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.

  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build

  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),

ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 981
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/981
- **Title**: fix(#974): Load earlier only when earlier pages exist (and at scroll top)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-974` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +192
- **Deletions**: -70
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T12:23:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T13:00:07Z

## PR Description

Fixes #974

## Root cause
Two layers combined to pin the sticker on every session:

1. **Host contract** (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`): full-open (non-windowed) sessions never ran `_refreshHistoryAbove` (early-returns when there is no `WindowedSessionStorage`), so `historyAboveCount` stayed `null` forever. `FaChatService`'s documented contract says hosts without paging surface report `0`. With `null`, `_topBannerVisible` treated 'count unknown' as 'show banner' — a first-message session therefore showed 'Load earlier'.
2. **Reveal-on-top** (`packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/fa_chat_screen.dart`): the pinned top banner rendered at every scroll position, even when pages do exist but the user sits at the live tail.

## Fix
1. Full-open sessions now report `historyAboveCount => _windowed == null ? 0 : _historyAboveCount` — the complete-transcript `0`; the banner never renders on them (data-driven pages-exist gate at the source).
2. `fa_ui` adds a reveal-on-top gate: the top banner renders only while the viewport sits within 64 px of the oldest edge (`pixels >= maxScrollExtent - 64` on the reversed list) or the transcript fits the viewport. Wired via the scroll controller listener plus a `ScrollMetricsNotification` listener (layout-time extent changes — first list attach, paged-in pages — never move the scroll position); re-measured post-frame after each message sync. Issue #223's empty-session escape and the E6 terminal 'Beginning of session' state are preserved.

**Tradeoff**: the pages-exist gate alone would have been acceptable per the issue; the scroll-top reveal was cheap because the screen already tracks the transcript's scroll controller, so both layers shipped. One-frame settle: the banner hides on the frame after the transcript's first layout measures its extents.

## Evidence
- **fail-pre** (base lib + HEAD tests): host contract test `Expected: <0> / Actual: <null>` (the reported bug, pinned); `UT-974-reveal` fails (banner visible at tail).
- **passes-post**: fa_ui `fa_chat_history_banner_test` 19/19 (×3 runs, incl. new `UT-974-first-msg` — the first-message repro — and `UT-974-reveal` hide→show→hide); flutter_app `agent_service_windowed_test` + `session_oversized_windowed_test` 14/14 (E2E updated: banner reveals on scroll-to-top, pages up, terminal state re-reveals at the new oldest edge); `chat_screen_test` + `l10n_guard_test` 11/11.
- No new user-facing strings (l10n guard clean); no pixel changes — chat goldens fail identically on base and HEAD in this sandbox (font antialiasing, verified same 2.60%/14019px diff on base), no golden regeneration needed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` clean on both changed libs; no CI dispatched.

+  /// slack of it. A transcript that fits the viewport (or has not laid
+  /// out yet) has no scroll range and always reveals.
+  bool get _revealedNow {

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
